diagnosis.summary: product-service is experiencing severe tail-latency degradation, with p95 response times rising from 6 ms to 1,586 ms over the past 4 minutes. DynamoDB read throttle events on the product-service table have climbed from 0 to 1,400 per minute, and a 0.4% 5xx error rate has appeared. Request rate is flat at 15.1 rps against a baseline of 15.0 rps.
diagnosis.root_cause: DynamoDB read throttling on the product-service table is the most likely root cause, with consumed read capacity at 11,900 RCU/min against a baseline of 480 RCU/min and 1,400 read throttle events per minute coinciding with the p95 database latency and end-to-end latency spikes.
evidence: p95 end-to-end latency rose from 6 ms to 1,586 ms, a 264x increase, while p50 latency remained nearly flat at 6 ms against a baseline of 5 ms, indicating tail requests are severely affected while the median is not.
p95 database latency rose from 4 ms to 1,580 ms, closely tracking the end-to-end p95 spike.
Read throttle events on the product-service table jumped from 0 to 1,400 per minute.
Consumed read capacity rose from 480 RCU/min to 11,900 RCU/min, a 24.8x increase.
The 5xx error rate is now 0.4% against a baseline of 0.0%.
Request rate is flat at 15.1 rps against a baseline of 15.0 rps.
recommended_actions: Immediately increase provisioned read capacity units on the product-service DynamoDB table, or switch the table to on-demand capacity mode to absorb the current 11,900 RCU/min load.
Enable DynamoDB auto-scaling on the product-service table so read capacity adjusts automatically to demand spikes.

Investigate recent changes to read access patterns on the product-service table, such as table scans or large batch reads, that could account for the 24.8x jump in consumed read capacity without a corresponding traffic increase.
Add a caching layer such as DynamoDB Accelerator in front of the product-service table to reduce direct DynamoDB read pressure for frequently accessed items.
Set CloudWatch alarms on read_throttle_events and db_consumed_read_capacity for the product-service table to detect future throttling before it affects p95 latency.
